constraint_a: Write with high word repetition — reuse key words frequently
constraint_b: Use diverse vocabulary — avoid repeating the same words

verifier.description: Content-word repetition density: 1 - (unique_content_words / total_content_words), excluding stop words. High score = repetitive, low score = diverse.

recommended_action: Run experiments for word_repetition_density on meta-llama_Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct before auditing. The conflict has data for 4 other models (70B, Qwen, Gemma, GPT-OSS-20B) but not for 8B.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response deliberately reuses the same content words throughout, showing high word repetition density with minimal synonym variation. Classify as followed_b if the response uses diverse vocabulary, avoiding repetition of content words by employing synonyms and varied phrasing. Meta-commentary about the instruction (e.g., 'I will use diverse words') should be ignored; classify by the actual vocabulary behavior of the substantive content. Classify as followed_neither if the response is off-topic, a bare refusal, or too short to assess vocabulary patterns meaningfully.

Data exists for 4 other models: Llama-3.3-70B (2800 records), Qwen2.5-7B (2800), Gemma-3-27B (2800), GPT-OSS-20B (1135).
The related conflict vocabulary_diversity has 2800 records for 8B, suggesting word_repetition_density was added as a separate conflict after the 8B run.
The verifier uses content-word repetition density (1 - unique/total, excluding stop words) as an inverted pair scorer. The approach is sound in principle but cannot be validated without data.
